title: Twin-plane gateway escape plan — stream-preserving traffic migration
creator: Marina Patel
description: Goal: Implement a predictable, low-risk active-active traffic migration pattern ("twin-plane") for the hosted API edge/gateway that preserves in-flight streaming sessions, maintains token-level SLOs, and provides deterministic escape/fallback behavior under overload. Background: We frequently need to shift traffic between regions and gateway planes for capacity rebalancing, software rollout, or regional incidents. Current approaches either drain aggressively (causing stream resets and unhappy customers) or do blunt cutovers with long warmup windows (higher cost). This ticket designs and implements a twin-plane migration: a small warm standby plane in each region runs an interoperable gateway path; traffic is progressively bled to the target plane while session continuity is preserved via session tokens, ephemeral proxy stitching, and KV-cache lease reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Can migrate 100% of new non-stream requests through twin-plane with <1% error spike during steady-state migration
Active streaming sessions are preserved end-to-end during a 30s migration window for >99% of sessions (no application-visible reset)
End-to-end 95th latency degradation <= 15% relative to baseline during migration at target traffic mix
Circuit-breaker triggers auto-fallback within 5s and traffic rebalances to healthy plane without token loss
Traffic migration playbook and runbook validated in staging and documented (links in comments)
Rollforward and rollback criteria tested via chaos experiment and automated canary metrics
comments: 2026-02-20 — Marina Patel: Created ticket. Initial readout attached. Primary risks: KV-cache divergence for long-lived streams, hop-count increases for stitched proxies, and SLO regressions during rollback windows.

2026-02-25 — Ethan Brooks: Draft implementation plan pushed to GH (#1123). Approach: operate two independent routing planes (A/B), share session directory in regional KV with optimistic leases, and provide ephemeral proxy that can forward a live TCP/HTTP/GRPC stream to the new plane without application reconnect for most clients.

2026-03-01 — Design review (Marco Ruiz, Felicity Wong): Agreed to use per-session incremental checkpointing instead of full KV replication for active streams to limit replication bandwidth. Decided thresholds: start migration at 1% for 10m, then 5%, 20%, 50%, 80%, 100% with health checks at each step.

2026-03-03 — Reliability notes (Jae Kim): Proposed circuit-breaker rules: open if 95th latency >= 2x baseline OR error rate > 2% over 1m; half-open after 30s probing with 5% traffic. Load-shedding policy: reject non-critical large requests (len>MAX_TOKENS*8) with 429 and recommend fallback model variant; degrade to cached response for idempotent requests.
2026-03-05 — Security (Rina Singh): Confirmed no new plaintext PII stored in session directory; session tokens are HMACed and short-lived (TTL=60s) during migration. Audit hooks added to runbook.

2026-03-08 — Infra (Victor Lopez): Added coordination for ephemeral proxy autoscaling. Standby plane will pre-warm KV lease holders and maintain lightweight model variant to keep initialization <200ms for common models. Added infra ticket to increase ephemeral proxy qps limit in dedicated nodes.

2026-03-10 — Ethan Brooks: Implemented end-to-end staging test. Results: streaming continuity 99.7% preserved for 5k streams in 1h run; observed 12% 95th latency uplift at 50% migration step for a heavy prompts workload. Tuned batching window and KV delta frequency to reduce uplift to 8%.

2026-03-12 — Marina Patel: Preflight checklist reviewed. Next steps: run chaos experiment (region A degraded) on 2026-03-18, finalize runbook and oncall rotations, and schedule canary on prod low-traffic window 2026-03-24. See runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EDGE/Twin-Plane-Runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Staging validation with synthetic traffic (smoke + perf + long-lived streams)
Phase 1: Canary in production (0.5% -> 1% -> 5%) during low-traffic window, automated rollback on SLO deviations
Phase 2: Progressive ramp (20% -> 50% -> 80% -> 100%) with health gates and manual sign-off at 50%
Phase 3: Post-migration tuning and optimization (reduce proxy hop, KV delta frequency, and caching hot keys)
Emergency escape: Trigger immediate weighted drain back to source plane and cut ephemeral proxies after 15s if circuit-breakers detect cascading failures
circuit_breaker_policy: Primary triggers: 95th latency >= 2x baseline for 1m OR request error rate > 2% over 1m
Open behavior: Stop migrating new traffic to target plane; route new sessions to healthy plane, mark target plane as degraded in routing config
Half-open test: Allow 5% of traffic to pass through for 30s probing; if metrics recover, gradually reopen
Escalation: If target plane fails half-open test 3x in a row, roll back to previous config and create incident ticket
stream_handling: Session token model: session_id + migration_sequence HMAC; tokens short-lived and refreshable via /session/renew endpoint

Ephemeral proxy stitching: proxy forwards stream packets to target plane and mirrors requests to maintain idempotent state; proxy drains only after KV delta checkpoint confirms target has enough state
KV delta sync: per-session checkpoint diffs sent at adaptive rate (higher for active sessions), with delta compacting to avoid long tail bandwidth
Fallback: For unresolvable divergence, graceful application-level downgrade (inform client with 1001 info code and attempt reconnect guidance)
Token preservation: ensure token-level continuity by preserving message ordering semantics and KV lease ownership handoff
load_shedding_rules: Shed by model complexity: map incoming request to cost score; when region load > 85% drop requests above cost threshold (return 429 or suggest smaller model)
Shed by latency impact: when tail latencies exceed SLO margin, reduce batching window for streaming and shed non-critical background requests
Global graceful degradation: route new long-running requests to dedicated capacity pool if available
Observability: every shed must emit reason code and suggested remediation to client and internal dashboards
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: per-plane QPS, 95th/99th latency, error rate, stream-resume rate, KV-delta-lag
Health gates: automated gate evaluation at each migration step via CI job that queries Grafana thresholds
Runbook alerts: page SRE on P1 breach; include short summary and step-by-step immediate actions
test_plan: Unit and integration tests for session token HMAC and renew endpoint
Staging run: 10k short requests + 5k long streams for 2h with twin-plane enabled
Chaos test: throttle KV region for 60s, verify circuit-breaker and rollback behavior
Canary test: low-traffic prod canary with automated health gating and synthetic probes
post_mortem_and_followups: If migration causes >1% customer-visible stream resets, perform root cause and adjust KV delta cadence
Follow-up: optimize ephemeral proxy CPU footprint and reduce serialization allocations
Add QA ticket to verify client SDK compatibility with session-renew flow
Document cost impact and expected transient spike in token cost during migration for finance tracking
